sup:70710.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We are pleased to submit our offer at a price of €6.05 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some insight into our cost environment: AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear customer,
Thank you very much for your message - it is always a pleasure to hear from you, and we are glad to help wherever we can.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.79 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 12 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
A few words on this from our side.
We checked the index change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.
We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.
That is not our reality: our AS-14404 is covered at fixed prices until March 2027, so that fall does not reach our cost.
AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. That remains.
LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. That remains.
PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. That remains.
We are pleased to accept the AS-14404 index clause to provide you with market-reflective pricing going forward.
Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: €5.73 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
Our standard Zahlungsziel is 30 days net.
We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.
We look forward to doing good business together, and our team is always there for you.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account. By extending the contract term to 24 months as you proposed, we gain planning stability which we are happy to pass on to you. 

We therefore propose €5.64 per unit, keeping the 90-day payment terms and the AS-14404 index clause. For our complete offer, we are pleased to state a price of €5.64 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, and a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404. We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

Dear customer,

We thank you for your revised offer and the proposed 36-month contract term. 

While we gladly accept the 36-month duration to grant you a better price, we cannot agree to a fixed price over such a long period and must retain the AS-14404 index clause. Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C. We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.

We therefore propose €5.47 per unit, keeping the 90-day payment terms and the index clause. To summarize our Angebot, we present a price of €5.47 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 36 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.

This is our final offer (letztes Angebot). Please decide. Our offer stays valid for 7 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Georg Aigner
Inside Sales, Edelstahl-Service Donautal GmbH

decisions.tactician: E0 and o9 carry the lowest C only because of their longer terms, and the term sheet credits contract length to it at zero. o6 meets its strong clause need at the lowest cost to us of any clause option (€4,300 over the horizon). It is also as valuable to the supplier as the other options on the list, and its C is close to the best twelve-month mixes. That should draw a constructive counter rather than a rejection of a bare deep cut. Contract length stays in reserve as a later concession to trade for price, and the cited arguments rebut its twelve-month index framing.

decisions.tactician: o9 meets its strongest need, the index clause it already accepts, and adds a two-year commitment that serves its planning need. Its price is at the engine's level, and our C (€999,623) stays close to the best no-clause options. The no-clause options o1/o2 save only about €5k of C but drop the term it values most, which invites a hard counter and slows the pace. E0's 36 months carries the same C but locks us in longer for no gain. Citing a2 (rising forecast) supports the volume need, while the 88 % delivery record (a1) would be confrontational right now.

decisions.tactician: o8 gives the supplier what it values most: a tighter index deadband, worth about 1.3 % to it against 0.4 % for the current 5 % deadband. On paper our C is essentially level with E0 (1,020,104 vs 1,020,528), so we gain no cost but offer a concession aimed at its core need, which makes acceptance or a near-price counter more likely. The no-clause options look cheaper for us, but dropping the clause it explicitly wants invites resistance. A db 0 % clause (o7) gives the supplier the most protection but costs us more in index exposure. The scorecard argument supports pushing price down without using up any argument kind the supplier has already heard. Accepting €5.64 now would leave clear value on the table given its pace of concessions.

decisions.tactician: o2 has the lowest C of all options (€1,028,315, tied with o1), well below E0 (€1,033,526) and the standing offer (€1,064,206). It is worth to the supplier the same as E0 (-2.9 %). The 36-month term addresses its planning-security and volume needs, which the 'to it' figure does not count, so o2 should be more attractive to it than o1. Dropping the clause removes the index risk cost from our side. Its hedge until March 2027 limits its near-term alloy exposure, so a long fixed price is plausible for it. At its recent pace it should meet us within about one reply.
